extracted.intended_audience: Colorado ELA educators and standardized-test scorers (grades 6-8)
extracted.subtask_description: Scoring rubric for Colorado Measures of Academic Success (CMAS) prose constructed-response items (Research Simulation, Literary Analysis, and Narrative Tasks) for grades 6–8; describes performance levels (score points 4–0) for multiple constructs and conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehension of ideas (explicit and inferential)
rubrics_metrics.description: demonstrates full comprehension of ideas stated explicitly and inferentially by providing an accurate analysis
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score point 4: demonstrates full comprehension of ideas stated explicitly and inferentially by providing an accurate analysis. Score point 3: demonstrates comprehension of ideas stated explicitly and/or inferentially by providing a mostly accurate analysis. Score point 2: demonstrates basic comprehension of ideas stated explicitly and/or inferentially by providing a generally accurate analysis. Score point 1: demonstrates limited comprehension of ideas stated explicitly and/or inferentially by providing a minimally accurate analysis. Score point 0: demonstrates no comprehension of ideas by providing an inaccurate or no analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addressing the prompt (task/purpose/audience appropriateness)
rubrics_metrics.description: addresses the prompt and provides development of the claim or topic that is appropriate to task, purpose, and audience
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score point 4: addresses the prompt and provides effective and comprehensive development of the claim or topic that is consistently appropriate to task, purpose, and audience. Score point 3: addresses the prompt and provides mostly effective development of claim or topic that is mostly appropriate to task, purpose, and audience. Score point 2: addresses the prompt and provides some development of claim or topic that is somewhat appropriate to task, purpose, and audience. Score point 1: addresses the prompt and provides minimal development of claim or topic that is limited in its appropriateness to task, purpose, and audience. Score point 0: is undeveloped and/or inappropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development of claim/topic (depth and completeness)
rubrics_metrics.description: provides development of the claim or topic (effective/comprehensive to minimal/undeveloped)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score point 4: provides effective and comprehensive development of the claim or topic. Score point 3: provides mostly effective development. Score point 2: provides some development. Score point 1: provides minimal development. Score point 0: is undeveloped and/or inappropriate. Development should be consistent with the prompt and appropriate to task/purpose/audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of reasoning and text-based evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: uses clear reasoning supported by relevant text-based evidence in the development of the claim or topic
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score point 4: uses clear reasoning supported by relevant text-based evidence. Score point 3: uses mostly clear reasoning supported by relevant text-based evidence. Score point 2: uses some reasoning and text-based evidence. Score point 1: uses limited reasoning and text-based evidence. Score point 0: includes little to no text-based evidence and/or inaccurate reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization and coherence
rubrics_metrics.description: is effectively organized with clear and coherent writing (to minimally organized/ incoherent)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score point 4: is effectively organized with clear and coherent writing. Score point 3: is organized with mostly clear and coherent writing. Score point 2: demonstrates some organization with somewhat coherent writing. Score point 1: demonstrates limited organization and coherence. Score point 0: lacks organization and coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style (establishment and maintenance of appropriate style)
rubrics_metrics.description: establishes and maintains an effective style (from effective to inappropriate)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score point 4: establishes and maintains an effective style. Score point 3: establishes and maintains a mostly effective style. Score point 2: has a style that is somewhat effective. Score point 1: has a style that is minimally effective. Score point 0: has an inappropriate style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Command of conventions of standard English
rubrics_metrics.description: demonstrates command of the conventions of standard English at an appropriate level of complexity (mechanics, grammar, usage)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score point 4: demonstrates full command of the conventions of standard English at an appropriate level of complexity; may be a few minor errors but meaning is clear. Score point 3: demonstrates some command; errors may occasionally impede understanding but meaning is generally clear. Score point 2: demonstrates limited command; errors often impede understanding. Score point 1/0: does not demonstrate command at the appropriate level; frequent and varied errors in mechanics, grammar, and usage impede understanding. (These statements appear across score levels for both RST/LAT and NT constructs.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative elements and development (Narrative Task)
rubrics_metrics.description: is developed with narrative elements and is appropriate to the task (development ranges from effectively developed to undeveloped)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score point 4 (NT): is effectively developed with narrative elements and is consistently appropriate to the task; effectively organized with clear and coherent writing and establishes and maintains an effective style. Score point 3: mostly effectively developed with narrative elements and mostly appropriate. Score point 2: developed with some narrative elements and generally appropriate. Score point 1: minimally developed with few narrative elements and limited appropriateness. Score point 0: is undeveloped and/or inappropriate to the task; lacks organization and coherence; has an inappropriate style. Per CCSS, narrative elements for grades 6–8 may include establishing a context, situating events in a time and place, developing a point of view, and developing characters’ motives (in addition to grades 3–5 elements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading dimension applicability for narratives
rubrics_metrics.description: the reading dimension is not scored for elicited narrative stories
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural note: For elicited narrative tasks (NT), the reading comprehension dimension is not scored; scoring focuses on written expression and conventions. This is an explicit exception in the rubric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment linkage to grade-level writing standards (coherence/clarity/cohesion)
rubrics_metrics.description: the elements of coherence, clarity, and cohesion to be assessed are expressed in the grade-level standards for writing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NOTE: The elements of coherence, clarity, and cohesion to be assessed are expressed in the grade-level standards 1–4 for writing. For narrative tasks, the elements to be assessed are expressed in grade-level standards 3 for writing. Scorers should reference grade-level standards when evaluating these aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone assessment limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: tone is not assessed in grade 6
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructional note: For grade 6 responses, tone is explicitly excluded from assessment; scorers should not evaluate or penalize based on tone for that grade.
